blocks.content: Valley glaciers originate in high mountain basins and flow downwards through pre-existing valleys under the force of gravity.

rows: Vast ice sheets covering entire continents or islands
Confined within steep mountain valley walls
Unconstrained outward flow in all directions
Linear downward flow guided by underlying topography
Antarctic Ice Sheet, Greenland Ice Sheet
Siachen Glacier, Gangotri Glacier, Baltoro Glacier
Cirques, arêtes, horns, hanging valleys, moraines

items: UPSC often asks to differentiate between landforms carved by alpine glaciers (cirques, arêtes, hanging valleys) vs. continental ice sheets (eskers, drumlins).
Remember that Siachen Glacier in the Karakoram Range is the longest glacier in India and the second-longest non-polar glacier in the world.
Malaspina Glacier in Alaska is the classic textbook example of a Piedmont glacier frequently asked in geographical landform questions.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Continental glaciers cover broad landmasses, flowing outwards in all directions regardless of underlying topography.
Valley or alpine glaciers originate in high mountain basins and flow downwards through mountain valleys.
Piedmont glaciers form when valley glaciers emerge from mountain canyons and spread out into broad lobes on flat lowlands.
Cirque glaciers occupy steep bowl-shaped mountain hollows and are often the birthplace of larger valley glaciers.
